extracted.intended_audience: parliamentarians, administrative agencies, policymakers, and legal drafters concerned with federal administrative procedure and rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and recommended statutory standards for federal independent administrative agencies on procedural fairness, rulemaking, participation, powers, and institutional oversight to guide agency rules of procedure and parliamentary supervision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency should ensure that interested persons (that is, those whose interests may be affected or who are in a position to contribute) are given reasonable and adequate notice of its proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines 'interested persons' as those affected or able to contribute; emphasizes notice must be reasonable and adequate so participants can prepare and participate meaningfully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to participate
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency should accord those who are sufficiently interested to be entitled to receive notice of a proceeding the right to participate by providing them with a reasonable opportunity to have their information and views made known to the agency, including their views on the submissions of other participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation includes ability to present information and respond to others' submissions; standard is a 'reasonable opportunity' rather than absolute entitlement in every form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to procedural information and assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency should provide interested persons with reasonable access to information about agency procedures and with reasonable assistance in complying with them, for example in the completion of forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should make procedural rules and practical help available to participants to reduce barriers to effective participation (e.g., help completing forms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to representation
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency should allow a participant to employ a representative whose specialized services can reasonably assist him to participate in an agency proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes that representation (legal or specialized) may be necessary for fair participation; agencies should permit representatives where reasonable assistance is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure to participants of relevant information
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency should ensure the disclosure to participants of all information that is relevant to the decision the agency will make, subject to reasonable accommodation for confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure duty is broad but balanced against confidentiality needs; disclosure promotes congruence of decision with record and assists review rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality and conflict-of-interest rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency should be impartial in carrying out its duties as a statutory decision maker. Members should be required, while holding office, to divest their conflicting financial interests, to disclose those of their spouses and close relatives, and to withdraw from individual proceedings whenever, for any reason, there is a reasonable apprehension of bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes detailed principles: eligibility need not depend on spouses' divestment but spouse/relative interests should be publicly disclosed; members aware of relatives' financial interests must disclose and may be required to withdraw from files; breaches should be judicially enforceable by persons with standing but should not automatically vitiate all agency decisions — challenges only where bias or realistic apprehension of bias is shown; member should withdraw unless participants consent and no other conflict rule violated; provision for ad hoc replacements where withdrawal would deprive quorum; rule against bias should not be used to delay proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Giving reasons for adverse decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency should give reasons for a decision whenever the decision amounts to a total or partial denial of a requested action, or is otherwise adverse to the interests of a participant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons encourage careful thought, tie decisions to the record, assist appeals and parliamentary accountability. Reasons should be issued simultaneously with the decision (not only on request). The report rejects legislating an 'adequacy' standard (to avoid uncertainty), noting that instituting a requirement to give reasons will tend to improve quality of reasons; reasons must be more than mere summary in some cases and must be clear enough to determine grounds and rational character of decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide for reconsideration and internal review
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency should provide for the reconsideration or review of its decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reconsideration/internal review can enhance consistency and correct mistakes (useful where decision-making is decentralized), but must emphasize getting it right initially; constraints may be needed (prescribed grounds, time-limits, defined participation rights) to protect legitimate expectations, manage time/cost burdens, and account for implications for external review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to secure relevant information (summons witnesses/documents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parliament should empower agencies with the power to secure information that is relevant to the matter in question, including the power to summon witnesses and documents during any proceeding at which a decision must be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Necessary for effective fact-finding; cites statutory precedents (e.g., Statutory Powers Procedure Act (Ont.), Administrative Procedure Act (U.S.) s. 555).

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to maintain control and remove disruptive persons
rubrics_metrics.description: Parliament should empower agencies with the power to maintain control over its proceedings and to remove disruptive persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should have authority to issue orders and instructions reasonably necessary to ensure the integrity of proceedings (e.g., administrative housekeeping powers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to initiate contempt proceedings in Federal Court
rubrics_metrics.description: Parliament should empower agencies with the power to initiate contempt proceedings in the Federal Court of Canada.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission prefers contempt handled as civil matters and recommends agencies be authorized to initiate contempt in Federal Court rather than imposing criminal penalties; to be dealt with like civil contempt of court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to compel preliminary sessions
rubrics_metrics.description: Parliament should empower agencies with the power to compel preliminary sessions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary sessions help organize proceedings and manage participation; included among powers to facilitate effective and efficient procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to adjourn proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Parliament should empower agencies with the power to adjourn proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjournment power is a routine procedural tool to manage cases and fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to make interim orders and provide interim relief
rubrics_metrics.description: Parliament should empower agencies with the power to make interim orders and to provide interim relief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interim relief provides practical protection of interests pending final decision and supports flexibility in administrative action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to adjust from adjudicative to rule‑making format
rubrics_metrics.description: Parliament should empower agencies with the power to adjust from an adjudicative to a rule-making format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes hybrid functions of agencies; allows processes to be tailored (e.g., switch to rule‑making where more appropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to add participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Parliament should empower agencies with the power to add participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits agencies to include additional interested parties where necessary to protect interests or ensure comprehensive deliberation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to consolidate proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Parliament should empower agencies with the power to consolidate proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consolidation can increase efficiency and consistency where multiple related matters exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules of evidence — court rules not generally required
rubrics_metrics.description: Except where otherwise specifically prescribed by statute, an agency should not be obliged to follow the rules of evidence that apply in courts of law, other than the rules of evidentiary privilege. Rules of evidence should be developed by agencies as incidents of administrative procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may develop administrative evidence rules suitable to their functions; only privilege rules are retained from court practice unless statute says otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic adoption and review of rules of procedure by agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should be encouraged to make and review periodically rules of procedure, using the legislated standards as guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parliament should refrain from inserting detailed procedural requirements in agency legislation; standards should guide agency rulemaking so agencies can adapt to operational needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parliamentary scrutiny and disallowance of agency rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules of procedure an agency adopts should be subject to scrutiny by a parliamentary committee, and to disallowance in Parliament, but not to judicial review on grounds of non-conformity with the standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee scrutiny and political disallowance provide democratic oversight; the standards operate as guidelines and non-conformity is not intended to be justiciable under ultra vires doctrine, though courts retain authority over conflicts with other legislation or constitutional rights and to determine whether agencies followed their own rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory body to assess agency draft rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An advisory body comprising representatives of public and private sector institutions having an interest in the federal administrative process should be required to file with the parliamentary committee that considers a set of agency rules of procedure a report of its assessment of the appropriateness of these rules. This report should be filed through a politically responsible official such as the Attorney General.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisory body plays an advisory and screening role in the rulemaking process; it should cooperate with agencies and stakeholders and its support should be a weighty factor though it lacks veto power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draft rules subject to notice and comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft rules should be subject to notice and comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advance warning systems (notice and comment) are recommended to ensure rules conform to legislative design and to bring public/institutional input into procedural rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop non‑binding model rules of procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Work should be undertaken to develop a series of model rules of procedure that would accommodate different decision‑making styles and activities. These models should serve as the starting‑point for the development of rules of procedure by any newly created agency, and for periodic review by an existing one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model rules would cover various decision-making situations (formal adjudication, many interveners, rulemaking, inquisitorial, file proceedings), incorporate best practices, be non‑binding, and help reduce unnecessary procedural diversity; agencies would be encouraged to borrow from models and would bear political onus to justify deviations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political onus to justify deviations from model rules
rubrics_metrics.description: To help eliminate unnecessary diversity in federal administrative procedure, agencies should have the political onus, when adopting rules of procedure, to justify deviations from the model rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rather than judicial enforcement, agencies must politically justify departures from model procedures to their parliamentary overseers and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve institutional information‑sharing and coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Further work should be undertaken towards improving the information sharing, education, consultation, screening and co‑ordination that are required for an integrated procedural framework for agency decision making at the federal level. In this respect, further consideration should be given to the creation of a permanent administrative council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposes an administrative council or similar institutional focus to take on advisory/screening/co-ordination roles, training, consultation, and to support consistent procedural evolution across agencies.
